turns.zh: 通常那正是找我们的好时机。对，我们确实看到人因为这样的原因来联系。还有几年前一篇很有意思的论文，显示不被察觉的认知能力衰退可能造成严重问题，导致糟糕的财务决策。

turns.en: So death is one thing and leaving a less financially sophisticated spouse to figure it out. But cognitive decline is a whole other issue. We've seen people come to us as a hedge against that as well, which I think is another pretty interesting reason.
turns.zh: 死亡是一个维度——留下不那么精通财务的配偶来独自应对一切。但认知衰退是另一个完全不同的问题。我们也见过人来找我们是为了对冲这个风险，又是一个挺有意思的原因。

turns.en: The other thing I've heard from a ton of people, and I don't really know if this is the best way to do it, because like you said then, the sharks will be circling, but I've had a ton of people tell me that I'm not going to become a client, but I've written into my will that if I die, I want you to be the first phone call that my wife makes.
turns.zh: 还有一件事我从很多人那里听到过——我不知道这是不是最好的做法，因为如你所说'鲨鱼会围过来'——他们跟我说：'我不会成为你们的客户，但我在遗嘱里写了，如果我去世，你是我爱人应该打的第一个电话。'

turns.en: I'm always like, oh, that's the best time to do it. Maybe not the first phone call, but yeah. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Interesting comment. That's a huge responsibility.
turns.zh: 我总觉得——也许那才是最合适的时机。不一定是'第一个电话'，但……有意思的说法。这个责任太重大了。

turns.en: I mean, I think any advisor would really take that responsibility very seriously, right? I mean, that's a huge compliment. Huge compliment. To be told, I trust you with my family's finances when I'm gone.
turns.zh: 我觉得任何一位顾问都会非常认真地担起这种责任。这是巨大的褒奖——被人托付：'我不在了之后，我家人的财务就交给你了。'

turns.en: I've heard the same thing. In fact, I know people who have done that for sure. We'll cover quite a bit here. The questions we talked about drawn different bodies of research with distinct financial implications for couples.
turns.zh: 我也听到过同样的事。事实上我就认识真的这么做的人。好，我们今天聊了不少。刚才讨论的问题来自不同的研究文献，各自对夫妻有不同的财务含义。

turns.en: I think if we kind of step back and think about all of them, one clear pattern emergence, which is that the couples who are going to set themselves up the best financially and emotionally are the ones who approach finances of marriage as a team and have open communication.
turns.zh: 我觉得如果退后一步总览全部，一个清晰的模式浮现出来：在财务和情感上把婚姻经营得最好的夫妻，是把婚姻的财务当成一个团队来对待、并且保持开放沟通的那些。

turns.en: There are multiple ways that can be accomplished based on the stuff that we talked about, the research we talked about, understanding you and your partner's spending tendencies lets you understand where each of you are coming from, aligning on the legal implications of marriage for your situation and whether that's a prenup or the default through open conversation before the marriage makes a lot of sense, prioritizing shared experiences like a honeymoon
turns.zh: 实现方式可以有很多，就是我们聊过的那些研究给出的：了解你和伴侣的消费倾向，让你们明白彼此从哪里来；就婚姻对你的法律含义达成一致——是签婚前协议还是接受默认安排——婚前开诚布公地沟通，非常有道理；优先安排共同体验，比如蜜月，

turns.en: over material displays like a huge rock or lavish wedding, taking a joint approach to your finances or at least thinking about them as shared, even if they're not actually set up as joint accounts rather than maintaining separate financial lives or at the extreme secret financial lives in the case of financial infidelity and then ensuring that both partners are involved in financial decisions rather than delegating everything to one person,
turns.zh: 而非物质炫耀——巨大的钻戒或奢华的婚礼；对财务采取共同的方式——至少'视其为共同'，哪怕账户没有真的合并——而不是维持各过各的财务生活，极端情况甚至是'秘密的财务生活'，即金融不忠；并确保双方都参与财务决策，而不是把一切交给一个人——

turns.en: which empirically is often the male spouse at least based on some of the research that we looked at. Those are all pretty good ways I think to open lines of communication and make sure everybody's on the same page and on board with the household financial strategy.
turns.zh: ——而根据我们看的一些研究，经验上那个人往往是丈夫。这些都是打开沟通渠道、让双方处于同一频道、认同家庭财务策略的好方法。

turns.en: That's it. Any final comments? No. Should we go to the after show? So we have gotten some feedback that people miss the after show. The good old days when Cameron would tell us about the shows he was watching on Netflix.
turns.zh: 好，就说这些。还有什么想补充的吗？没有了。我们进番外（after show）吧。我们收到一些反馈，说大家怀念 after show——怀念当年 Cameron 给我们讲他在 Netflix 追什么剧的美好时光。

turns.en: We joke that there was six people who stuck around this long. Yeah, the six people in the after show. We do have a couple of reviews to read so we can go there.
turns.zh: 我们开玩笑说，能听到这里的也就六个人——对，番外就那六位老听众。我们手上确实有几条评论可以念，那就开始吧。

turns.en: I do also want to mention while we're here in the after show. We did an episode, a special episode on a Tuesday as opposed to a Thursday with two of the folks from one digital.
turns.zh: 在番外这里我还想顺便提一句：我们做了一期特别节目，改在周二而不是周四，是和 One Digital 的两位同事一起做的。那期节目不太受欢迎。

turns.en: The episode was not well received. So I just wanted to say they acknowledged. We heard the feedback. We saw the feedback. People were very willing to share their perspectives on how much they disliked that episode and the reasons why.
turns.zh: 所以我想说的是：我们认账。我们听到了反馈，也看到了反馈。大家非常不吝于表达他们多不喜欢那期节目，以及为什么不喜欢。

turns.en: That's kind of all I want to say about it. We saw the comments. We understand. The feedback is well taken. We'll move on from there. Yeah. A couple of reviews here.
turns.zh: 关于这个我就说这么多。我们看到评论了，我们理解，反馈照单全收。然后我们继续往前走。好，这里有几条评论。

We have a few reviews from Apple Podcast to read under SEC regulations were required to disclose whether a review which may be interpreted as a testimonial was left by a client, whether any direct or indirect compensation was paid for the review or whether there are any conflicts of interest related to the review.
turns.zh: 我先念免责声明。我们有几条 Apple Podcasts 上的评论要念。按照 SEC 的规定，我们必须披露：这条可被解读为推荐证言的评论是否出自客户；我们是否为该评论支付过任何直接或间接的报酬；以及是否存在与该评论相关的任何利益冲突。

turns.zh: 由于评论通常是匿名的，我们无法确认评论者是否为客户，也无从披露此类利益冲突。第一条，交给 Dan。

turns.en: Yeah. So this one is titled best financial show disclosure. I'm not affiliated. This is one of the best financial podcasts there is apical for both US and non US citizens, which is great because most of the podcasts are US citizen biased.
turns.zh: 好。这条的标题是《最好的理财节目——声明：我和你们没有关联》：'这是市面上最好的理财播客之一，

turns.en: The only downside of the podcast is that it makes you go into the rational reminder forums, install the deep dive, which is a never ending loop of learning, even for people like me.
turns.zh: 对美国公民和非美国公民都同样出色，这一点很棒，因为大多数播客都偏向美国公民。这个播客唯一的缺点是，它会让你点进 Rational Reminder 论坛、开始深挖——

turns.en: Not that savvy and who don't work in finance can't wait for the leverage podcast. And this is from VBENV 1992 from Israel. Very cool. The rational reminder community is the situation.
turns.zh: 那是一个永无止境的学习循环，对我这种不算精通、又不做金融的人也一样。等不及想听 leverage 那期了。'——来自以色列的 VBENV 1992。很酷。Rational Reminder 社群就是个'沉洞'。

turns.en: People can get sucked in there. Never ending loop. I do love that since we started doing a disclaimer for our reviews, people started adding disclaimers to their own reviews.
turns.zh: 人真的会被吸进去——永无止境。我很喜欢的一点是：自从我们开始给评论念免责声明，听众也开始给自己的评论加免责声明了。

turns.en: Okay, let's do the next one here. Great podcast. Thanks Ben and team. I've been listening to this podcast for years and look forward to my Thursday commute every week for the new RR episode.
turns.zh: 好，来念下一条。'很棒的播客，谢谢 Ben 和团队。我听这个节目好多年了，每周都期待周四通勤时收听新的 RR 节目。'

turns.en: I'd love to see an episode focused on optimal asset allocation and life cycle theory for defined benefit pensioners, of which I imagine there are certainly quite a few in Canada from the public service.
turns.zh: '我很想听一期专门讲固定收益（defined benefit）领取者的最优资产配置和生命周期理论——我猜加拿大公务员系统里这样的人相当不少。'

turns.en: PS, just to make this fun, I'll have you know that your podcast brings me such great comfort. I listened to it while I was getting minor surgery by moist towelette from Canada.
turns.zh: '附注：为了增添趣味，我要告诉你们，你们的播客给了我极大的安慰。我做小手术时都一边听它、一边用 moist towelette（湿巾）擦身。'——来自加拿大。'这可真是个名字。'是啊，这个名字很好笑，故事也很好笑。我来念下一条，'未来投资者'：

turns.en: That's quite the name. Nice. That's a very funny name and also a very funny story. I'll do the next one, future investor as a 22 year old mechanical engineering student and massive Excel nerd.
turns.zh: '我是一名 22 岁的机械工程专业学生，也是个超级 Excel 迷。

turns.en: This podcast is right at my alley. I transitioned here from the wealthy barber and Dave's podcast and the level of data-driven nerdy detail you guys provide is unmatched.
turns.zh: 你们的播客完全对我的胃口。我是从 The Wealthy Barber 和 Dave 的播客转过来的，你们提供的数据驱动、极客式的细节深度无人能及。

turns.en: Even though I have zero assets to invest yet, every episode gets me incredibly excited to graduate and start my financial journey. You guys make complex financial topics understandable and entertaining.
turns.zh: 虽然我现在还没有任何可投资的资产，但每一期都让我无比兴奋地想毕业、开始我的财务之旅。你们把复杂的金融话题讲得既易懂又有趣。

turns.en: Keep up the amazing work and that's by Gordy from Canada. All right, we'll wrap up with this last one, in-depth financial analysis. I found rational reminder from an interview on the Bogleheads on Investing podcast.
turns.zh: 继续保持了不起的工作。'——来自加拿大的 Gordy。好，最后一条收尾：'深度财务分析'：'我是在 The Bogleheads on Investing 播客的一期访谈里发现 Rational Reminder 的。'

turns.en: Since then, I've been going through the archive, excellent interviews and in-depth dives into the data, looking forward to the next 400 plus podcasts.
turns.zh: '从那以后我一直在翻你们的节目库。访谈出色，对数据的挖掘也非常深入。期待接下来 400 多期。'——来自美国的 E.F. Shuler。

turns.en: That's from E.F. Shuler from the US of A. Very nice. Hopefully, there will be 400 plus more to come. I mentioned the rational reminder community being a situation and how people can get sucked into it.
turns.zh: 太好了，希望后面真的有 400 多期。我刚才提到 Rational Reminder 社群是个'沉洞'、人会被吸进去。

turns.en: Looking at the all-time stats for the community in terms of time read, the time people spend reading topics on the community. One person spent three months, three months of their life reading topics.
turns.zh: 我去看了社群的历史累计统计——大家在主题帖上花掉的阅读时间。有一个人累计读了三个月——三个月的人生花在阅读帖子上。

turns.en: Time well spent. I hope so. That's the biggest outlier, but there's 67 days, 71 days, 49 days. Does it have your stat, Ben? 44 days. There you go.
turns.zh: 希望是值得的。这是最大的极端值，另外还有 67 天、71 天、49 天的。Ben，你有你的统计吗？——44 天。看吧。

turns.en: I'm near the top. I'm near the top, but not at the top, but I'm in the top 10% or so, maybe the top 5%. Nice. You can't actually sort it by day to read.
turns.zh: 我在前列，但不是最靠前——大概在 top 10%，也许 top 5%。

turns.en: I don't know why they don't let you do that. Because it would be too alarming? Maybe. Maybe. I can sort it by post-read. That seems like a pretty good proxy.
